approachQuestion.prompt:
Create a cyclic schedule containing every k-bit configuration exactly once, starting with zero. Consecutive configurations must differ in exactly one bit, including the last and first configurations. Return any such array.

Constraints: 1 <= k <= 20; one machine word holds a configuration and indices through 2^k.
Example: k=2 -> [0,1,3,2] is valid. Edge case: k=1 -> [0,1].

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: Logical shifts, XOR, indexing and writing one output word take constant time. A final output buffer of 2^k words can be allocated directly; its storage is excluded.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: For i from zero through 2^k-1, write i XOR (i logically shifted right by one) into output[i].
options.feedback: The reflected binary Gray mapping is a bijection and adjacent indices map to words differing in one bit, including the cyclic boundary.

options.text: Start output with [0]. For each bit position, append the current output in reverse index order with that bit set, reading the existing prefix directly in the final output buffer.
options.feedback: Reflection joins the halves through one new bit and preserves adjacency inside each half. Reading the same output buffer needs no additional sequence copy.

options.text: Return the integers from zero through 2^k-1 in increasing order.
options.feedback: For k=2, consecutive values 1 and 2 differ in two bits, so numeric order is not a valid schedule.

options.text: Allocate and retain a separate array of all binary indices, then create the output by applying i XOR (i shifted right by one) to each stored index.
options.feedback: The output is valid, but retaining a second full array is unnecessary; indices can be generated in order.

feedback.reason: The reflected mapping i XOR (i>>1) makes adjacent binary counter changes collapse to one changed output bit.
details: Allocate the final output buffer. For each index i, directly write i XOR (i shifted logically right by one). The reflected mapping changes one bit between adjacent indices and between the final entry and zero.

The reflected mapping i XOR (i>>1) makes adjacent binary counter changes collapse to one changed output bit. Include the final-to-zero adjacency because the schedule is cyclic. Direct generation avoids storing a separate reflected construction.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For index-to-gray, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let k be the number of configuration bits. Count output writes in time and exclude the final output array from auxiliary space.
constraints: Logical shifts, XOR, indexing and writing one output word take constant time. A final output buffer of 2^k words can be allocated directly; its storage is excluded.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

feedback.reason: One word formula and write per one of 2^k configurations.
details: There is one fixed-width formula evaluation and one output write per configuration. Beyond the output buffer, only the index and a temporary word are needed.
Logical shifts, XOR, indexing and writing one output word take constant time. A final output buffer of 2^k words can be allocated directly; its storage is excluded.
“O(k*2^k) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The formula uses a fixed number of word operations per index, not a scan of all k bits.
“O(2^k) time, O(2^k) auxiliary space”: That would include the excluded output buffer or the separate index-list alternative.
“O(k) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The output itself contains 2^k entries.
